article_content: (CNN) -- America has beaches, too. That's the message from the 2014 U.S. News & World Report 'World's Best Places to Visit' rankings for the United States. On the U.S. list, Maui jumped six places from last year's rankings to steal the top spot from Yellowstone National Park, which fell to second place. 'When we think about American vacations, people are less inclined to think of beach cities per se, at least before big cities like New York, Chicago or our National Parks,' said Allison Michaels, the site's travel editor. 'So it's interesting to see a beach destination rise to the top.' Washington D.C., San Francisco, and New York City rounded out the top five vacation destinations, whose rankings are based on a formula combining online reader votes with the opinion of reputable travel writers. Click through the gallery to see what you think of all 20 top spots.

Dalam senarai A.S., Maui melonjak enam tangga dari ranking tahun lepas untuk merampas kedudukan teratas daripada Taman Negara Yellowstone, yang jatuh ke tangga kedua. 'Apabila kita memikirkan tentang percutian di Amerika, orang ramai kurang cenderung untuk memikirkan bandar-bandar pantai, sekurang-kurangnya berbanding bandar-bandar besar seperti New York, Chicago atau Taman Negara kita,' kata Allison Michaels, editor pelancongan laman web tersebut. 'Jadi, menarik untuk melihat destinasi pantai mendaki ke tangga teratas.' Washington D.C., San Francisco, dan New York City melengkapkan senarai lima destinasi percutian terbaik, yang rankingnya berdasarkan formula yang menggabungkan undian pembaca dalam talian dengan pendapat penulis pelancongan yang bereputasi. Klik melalui galeri untuk melihat pendapat anda tentang kesemua 20 tempat teratas.

article_content: Washington (CNN) -- Same-sex marriage is becoming a less contentious issue in American politics. While perhaps not entirely a non-issue, it generates less intense controversy than when it was a reliable wedge issue. When Attorney General Eric Holder announced Saturday at the Human Rights Campaign's gala that the federal government would broaden its recognition of same-sex marriages in federal legal contexts, including bankruptcies, prison visitation, and survivor benefits, the political reaction was minimal. Social media discussion was subdued. Public statements from Republicans and Democrats were scarce. Sunday political talk shows barely mentioned the topic. The primary point of contention may be President Obama's use of executive action to advance his agenda, rather than the same-sex marriage issue itself. "This is a very significant development," stated Steve Elmendorf, a Democratic donor and former campaign manager for John Kerry's 2004 presidential campaign. Although Holder's announcement expands upon the Supreme Court's decision last year to strike down the Defense of Marriage Act, it firmly establishes the Obama administration's policy stance. "Similar to the civil rights movement of the 1960s, the stakes in this generation's fight for LGBT equality are immense," Holder stated. "As Attorney General, I will ensure this department is actively involved in this pivotal moment in history." Democratic Senator Richard Durbin commented on CBS' "Face the Nation" Sunday that the announcement was "logical, consistent, and passionate." However, the day after Holder's announcement, conservatives, generally opposed to same-sex marriage, offered limited commentary. Republican Senator Kelly Ayotte of New Hampshire remarked on CBS News' "Face the Nation" that it "appears to be another instance of the Obama administration imposing its will on the states," noting same-sex marriage is legal in her state. She suggested it "could" be an issue in states where it remains illegal, but stopped short of strong condemnation. Public opinion has substantially evolved, with a majority of Americans now supporting same-sex marriage. A national Quinnipiac University poll from September indicated 56% of Americans support marriage for same-sex couples, a significant increase from 25% in 1996. A 2010 CNN poll marked the first time a majority of respondents expressed support. Republican strategist Ana Navarro observed on CNN's "State of the Union" that opinions on same-sex marriage represent the "most rapid social change in our lifetime." Navarro indicated Republican politicians' positions are also changing, though they are not publicly vocal. She suggested that while Republican views are rapidly evolving, politicians may remain quiet to avoid political repercussions without immediate legislative action. Potential political backlash could arise from the party base, where opposition is more prevalent. The same Quinnipiac poll found that 36% of Republicans in their states support same-sex marriage. Navarro maintained that opinions are quickly shifting among Republican voters, and by the 2016 presidential election, it might be "much less of an issue." The past five years have witnessed significant change on this issue. Over a dozen states have legalized same-sex marriage, and Obama is the first president to endorse it. Support for gay rights generally has increased, evidenced by the Senate's passage last year of the Employment Non-Discrimination Act, prohibiting workplace discrimination based on sexual orientation. This marked the Senate's first passage of the measure, with 10 Republican votes. Republican strategist John Feehery, president of QGA Communications, stated: "The Republican Party should focus on numerous other issues. I anticipate they will not dedicate significant effort to opposing this issue." Elmendorf suggested the administration's decision posed no political risk for Obama or Democrats leading into the 2014 midterm elections. "There's no political downside for Obama. None," he asserted. Elmendorf noted that gay rights issues in politics are no longer a niche concern, appealing to a broad range of voters. "It's no longer solely about gay voters; it concerns any voter under 40," he explained. However, not all remained silent. Former Arkansas governor and potential 2016 Republican presidential candidate Mike Huckabee, appealing to social conservatives, emailed his supporters shortly after Holder's announcement. "Is it surprising this administration is selectively enforcing laws?" the email questioned. It included a link to the CNN story on Holder's announcement and requested support for Huckpac, his political action committee, and the Conservative Candidates fund. Same-sex marriage could become a campaign issue in more conservative districts and states, where incumbents might face right-wing challenges, especially in the over two dozen states with constitutional amendments banning same-sex marriage. A Republican operative suggested some might "perceive this as further overreach by the Obama administration to undermine their will." Even Obama's evolution on the issue, from opposition to support, has not fully satisfied LGBT activists and advocates. Notably, he has not indicated federal-level action to standardize same-sex marriage laws nationwide. While the reaction may be more muted, for proponents, the issue remains unresolved.
translated_content: Washington (CNN) -- Perkahwinan sesama jenis menjadi isu yang kurang kontroversi dalam politik Amerika. Walaupun mungkin tidak sepenuhnya isu yang tidak penting, ia menghasilkan kontroversi yang kurang sengit berbanding ketika ia menjadi isu pemecahbelah yang boleh diandalkan. Apabila Peguam Negara Eric Holder mengumumkan pada hari Sabtu di gala Kempen Hak Asasi Manusia bahawa kerajaan persekutuan akan meluaskan pengiktirafannya terhadap perkahwinan sesama jenis dalam konteks undang-undang persekutuan, termasuk kebankrapan, lawatan penjara, dan faedah orang terselamat, reaksi politik adalah minimum. Perbincangan media sosial adalah tenang. Kenyataan awam daripada Republikan dan Demokrat adalah jarang. Rancangan bual bicara politik Ahad hampir tidak menyebut topik itu. Perkara utama pertikaian mungkin adalah penggunaan tindakan eksekutif oleh Presiden Obama untuk memajukan agendanya, dan bukannya isu perkahwinan sesama jenis itu sendiri. "Ini adalah perkembangan yang sangat penting," kata Steve Elmendorf, seorang penderma Demokrat dan bekas pengurus kempen untuk kempen presiden John Kerry pada tahun 2004. Walaupun pengumuman Holder meluaskan keputusan Mahkamah Agung tahun lalu untuk membatalkan Akta Pertahanan Perkahwinan, ia dengan tegas menetapkan pendirian dasar pentadbiran Obama. "Sama seperti gerakan hak sivil tahun 1960-an, kepentingan dalam perjuangan generasi ini untuk kesaksamaan LGBT adalah besar," kata Holder. "Sebagai Peguam Negara, saya akan memastikan jabatan ini terlibat secara aktif dalam momen penting dalam sejarah ini." Senator Demokrat Richard Durbin mengulas di "Face the Nation" CBS pada hari Ahad bahawa pengumuman itu adalah "logik, konsisten, dan bersemangat." Namun, sehari selepas pengumuman Holder, konservatif, yang umumnya menentang perkahwinan sesama jenis, memberikan ulasan yang terhad. Senator Republikan Kelly Ayotte dari New Hampshire berkata di "Face the Nation" CBS News bahawa ia "nampaknya merupakan satu lagi contoh pentadbiran Obama memaksakan kehendaknya kepada negeri-negeri," sambil menyatakan perkahwinan sesama jenis adalah sah di negerinya. Beliau mencadangkan ia "boleh" menjadi isu di negeri-negeri di mana ia kekal haram, tetapi tidak memberikan kecaman yang kuat. Pendapat umum telah berkembang dengan ketara, dengan majoriti rakyat Amerika kini menyokong perkahwinan sesama jenis. Tinjauan Universiti Quinnipiac kebangsaan dari bulan September menunjukkan 56% rakyat Amerika menyokong perkahwinan untuk pasangan sesama jenis, peningkatan yang ketara daripada 25% pada tahun 1996. Tinjauan CNN pada tahun 2010 menandakan kali pertama majoriti responden menyatakan sokongan. Pakar strategi Republikan Ana Navarro memerhatikan di "State of the Union" CNN bahawa pendapat mengenai perkahwinan sesama jenis mewakili "perubahan sosial terpantas dalam hidup kita." Navarro menyatakan bahawa kedudukan ahli politik Republikan juga berubah, walaupun mereka tidak bersuara secara terbuka. Beliau mencadangkan bahawa walaupun pandangan Republikan berkembang pesat, ahli politik mungkin kekal senyap untuk mengelakkan kesan politik tanpa tindakan perundangan segera. Reaksi balas politik yang berpotensi boleh timbul daripada pangkalan parti, di mana penentangan lebih lazim. Tinjauan Quinnipiac yang sama mendapati bahawa 36% Republikan di negeri mereka menyokong perkahwinan sesama jenis. Navarro menegaskan bahawa pendapat dengan cepat berubah di kalangan pengundi Republikan, dan menjelang pilihan raya presiden 2016, ia mungkin "kurang menjadi isu." Lima tahun yang lalu telah menyaksikan perubahan yang signifikan mengenai isu ini. Lebih daripada sedozen negeri telah menghalalkan perkahwinan sesama jenis, dan Obama adalah presiden pertama yang menyokongnya. Sokongan untuk hak gay secara umum telah meningkat, dibuktikan dengan kelulusan Senat tahun lalu terhadap Akta Bukan Diskriminasi Pekerjaan, yang melarang diskriminasi di tempat kerja berdasarkan orientasi seksual. Ini menandakan kelulusan pertama Senat bagi langkah itu, dengan 10 undi Republikan. Pakar strategi Republikan John Feehery, presiden QGA Communications, menyatakan: "Parti Republikan harus memberi tumpuan kepada banyak isu lain. Saya menjangkakan mereka tidak akan menumpukan usaha yang besar untuk menentang isu ini." Elmendorf mencadangkan keputusan pentadbiran itu tidak menimbulkan risiko politik bagi Obama atau Demokrat menjelang pilihan raya pertengahan penggal 2014. "Tidak ada keburukan politik bagi Obama. Tiada," tegasnya. Elmendorf menyatakan bahawa isu hak gay dalam politik bukan lagi kebimbangan khusus, menarik minat pelbagai pengundi. "Ia bukan lagi semata-mata mengenai pengundi gay; ia melibatkan mana-mana pengundi di bawah 40 tahun," jelasnya. Bagaimanapun, tidak semua orang berdiam diri. Bekas gabenor Arkansas dan calon presiden Republikan 2016 yang berpotensi Mike Huckabee, yang menarik minat konservatif sosial, menghantar e-mel kepada penyokongnya sejurus selepas pengumuman Holder. "Adakah mengejutkan pentadbiran ini memilih dan menguatkuasakan undang-undang yang mereka suka?" e-mel itu mempersoalkan. Ia termasuk pautan ke cerita CNN mengenai pengumuman Holder dan meminta sokongan untuk Huckpac, jawatankuasa tindakan politiknya, dan dana Calon Konservatif. Perkahwinan sesama jenis boleh menjadi isu kempen di daerah dan negeri yang lebih konservatif, di mana penyandang jawatan mungkin menghadapi cabaran sayap kanan, terutamanya di lebih daripada dua sedozen negeri dengan pindaan perlembagaan yang melarang perkahwinan sesama jenis. Seorang pegawai Republikan mencadangkan sesetengah orang mungkin "melihat ini sebagai pencerobohan lebih lanjut oleh pentadbiran Obama untuk melemahkan kehendak mereka." Malah evolusi Obama mengenai isu ini, daripada penentangan kepada sokongan, tidak sepenuhnya memuaskan hati aktivis dan penyokong LGBT. Terutama, beliau tidak menunjukkan tindakan peringkat persekutuan untuk menyeragamkan undang-undang perkahwinan sesama jenis di seluruh negara. Walaupun reaksinya mungkin lebih senyap, bagi penyokong, isu itu kekal belum selesai.

article_content: If you've ever paid a lot for an airline ticket, you know it can be expensive. But this was different. Qantas Airlines Flight 94 to Melbourne had to turn back to Los Angeles about an hour into its trip Wednesday morning when a water pipe started leaking on the upper deck. The jet is an Airbus A380, the world's only complete double-decker airplane. Video footage showed water running down the aisle. The water leaked through the floor and affected passengers in economy class below. Crew members relocated passengers and provided blankets to keep them dry, the airline stated. Qantas assured that passengers were never in danger and are accommodating them in hotels while investigating the cause with Airbus.

Penerbangan Qantas Airlines 94 ke Melbourne terpaksa berpatah balik ke Los Angeles kira-kira sejam dalam perjalanannya pada pagi Rabu apabila paip air mula bocor di dek atas. Jet itu adalah Airbus A380, satu-satunya pesawat dua tingkat lengkap di dunia. Rakaman video menunjukkan air mengalir di lorong. Air itu bocor melalui lantai dan menjejaskan penumpang di kelas ekonomi di bawah. Anak kapal memindahkan penumpang dan menyediakan selimut untuk memastikan mereka kering, kata syarikat penerbangan itu. Qantas memberi jaminan bahawa penumpang tidak pernah dalam bahaya dan menempatkan mereka di hotel sambil menyiasat punca kejadian itu dengan Airbus.

article_content: Baghdad - On Monday, tens of thousands of followers of the anti-American Shiite cleric Muqtada al-Sadr demonstrated to mark the ninth anniversary of the U.S. invasion of Iraq. The protesters called for improvements in essential public services in the country, which has been struggling since the war. In the southern oil city of Basra, some demonstrators carried symbolic coffins labeled with 'electricity,' 'water,' and 'education.' Others displayed cables and empty water containers, visually representing their dissatisfaction with the ongoing lack of basic utilities. Iraqi security authorities estimated that between 100,000 and 120,000 individuals participated in the demonstration. Many carried Iraqi national flags, banners, and portraits of al-Sadr, the Shiite Muslim leader whose militia previously engaged in intense conflicts with U.S. forces. With the U.S. military withdrawal from Iraq now complete, the banners at the protest directly addressed Iraq's new political leadership, questioning, 'Where are your promises?' In a statement delivered on his behalf, al-Sadr advised his supporters to use their voting power if their demands were ignored by the government. 'If the government fails to listen to your demands, then you will decide what is best for you,' he stated. According to the Brookings Institution's Iraq Index, approximately 30% of Iraq's population lacks consistent access to clean drinking water, a significant increase from 2008. While electricity generation had surpassed pre-war levels by mid-2007, it still only met about 56% of the national demand in 2011, as per Brookings estimates. Al-Sadr, who rarely appears in public, also reiterated his call for his followers to maintain their firm stance against the United States and Israel. 'If we unite our voices, then we will be able to defeat America, Israel and other enemies,' Sheikh Assad al-Nassri conveyed to the assembled crowd, speaking for al-Sadr. The U.S.-led invasion of Iraq commenced on March 20, 2003, leading to the removal of long-time dictator Saddam Hussein. However, the invasion was followed by years of violence, initially from an insurgency of Hussein loyalists, and subsequently by sectarian conflict between the Shiite majority and Sunni minority. Al-Sadr's militia, the Mehdi Army, was implicated in some of the most severe episodes of violence. Although al-Sadr officially disbanded the group in 2008, he announced its transformation into a movement focused on opposing secularism and Western ideologies. Despite its militia disbandment, al-Sadr's political movement has become influential in Iraqi politics. Its 39 seats in the Iraqi parliament played a crucial role in Prime Minister Nuri al-Maliki securing a second term. While al-Sadr's supporters typically hold anniversary demonstrations in Baghdad, this year's event was relocated to Basra due to heightened security measures in the capital as it prepares to host an upcoming Arab summit, according to security officials. The United States initially justified the invasion by claiming that Saddam Hussein's regime possessed stockpiles of chemical and biological weapons, long-range missiles, and a nuclear weapons program. However, later inspections revealed that while Baghdad had attempted to conceal some weapons-related research, Iraq had been effectively disarmed under U.N. sanctions in the 1990s. The invasion quickly led to the downfall of Hussein, who was later executed for the mass killing of Shiite villagers following an assassination attempt in the 1980s. The conflict resulted in the deaths of nearly 4,500 American and over 300 allied soldiers before the final U.S. troop withdrawal in December. Estimates of Iraqi casualties exceed 100,000.
translated_content: Baghdad - Pada hari Isnin, berpuluh ribu pengikut ulama Syiah anti-Amerika, Muqtada al-Sadr, berdemonstrasi untuk menandakan ulang tahun kesembilan pencerobohan AS ke atas Iraq. Para penunjuk perasaan menyeru agar perkhidmatan awam yang penting di negara itu diperbaiki, kerana negara tersebut telah bergelut sejak perang. Di bandar minyak selatan Basra, beberapa demonstran membawa keranda simbolik yang dilabel dengan 'elektrik,' 'air,' dan 'pendidikan.' Yang lain mempamerkan kabel dan bekas air kosong, secara visual mewakili rasa tidak puas hati mereka terhadap kekurangan utiliti asas yang berterusan. Pihak berkuasa keselamatan Iraq menganggarkan bahawa antara 100,000 dan 120,000 individu menyertai demonstrasi tersebut. Ramai yang membawa bendera kebangsaan Iraq, sepanduk, dan potret al-Sadr, pemimpin Muslim Syiah yang militianya pernah terlibat dalam konflik sengit dengan pasukan AS. Dengan pengunduran tentera AS dari Iraq yang kini selesai, sepanduk di perhimpunan itu secara langsung ditujukan kepada kepimpinan politik baharu Iraq, mempersoalkan, 'Di mana janji-janji kamu?' Dalam satu kenyataan yang disampaikan bagi pihaknya, al-Sadr menasihati penyokongnya untuk menggunakan kuasa undi mereka jika tuntutan mereka diabaikan oleh kerajaan. 'Jika kerajaan gagal mendengar tuntutan kamu, maka kamu akan memutuskan apa yang terbaik untuk kamu,' katanya. Menurut Indeks Iraq Institut Brookings, kira-kira 30% penduduk Iraq tidak mempunyai akses yang konsisten kepada air minuman bersih, satu peningkatan yang ketara dari tahun 2008. Walaupun penjanaan elektrik telah melebihi paras pra-perang menjelang pertengahan tahun 2007, ia masih hanya memenuhi kira-kira 56% daripada permintaan negara pada tahun 2011, menurut anggaran Brookings. Al-Sadr, yang jarang muncul di khalayak ramai, juga mengulangi seruannya kepada penyokongnya untuk mengekalkan pendirian tegas mereka terhadap Amerika Syarikat dan Israel. 'Jika kita menyatukan suara kita, maka kita akan dapat mengalahkan Amerika, Israel dan musuh-musuh lain,' Sheikh Assad al-Nassri menyampaikan kepada orang ramai yang berkumpul, bagi pihak al-Sadr. Pencerobohan pimpinan AS ke atas Iraq bermula pada 20 Mac 2003, yang membawa kepada penyingkiran diktator lama Saddam Hussein. Walau bagaimanapun, pencerobohan itu diikuti oleh keganasan selama bertahun-tahun, bermula dengan pemberontakan oleh penyokong setia Hussein, dan seterusnya oleh konflik sektarian antara majoriti Syiah dan minoriti Sunni. Militia al-Sadr, Tentera Mehdi, terlibat dalam beberapa episod keganasan yang paling teruk. Walaupun al-Sadr secara rasmi membubarkan kumpulan itu pada tahun 2008, beliau mengumumkan transformasinya menjadi gerakan yang memberi tumpuan kepada menentang sekularisme dan ideologi Barat. Walaupun militianya telah dibubarkan, gerakan politik al-Sadr telah menjadi berpengaruh dalam politik Iraq. 39 kerusinya di parlimen Iraq memainkan peranan penting dalam memastikan Perdana Menteri Nuri al-Maliki memperoleh penggal kedua. Walaupun penyokong al-Sadr biasanya mengadakan demonstrasi ulang tahun di Baghdad, acara tahun ini telah dipindahkan ke Basra kerana langkah-langkah keselamatan yang dipertingkatkan di ibu negara ketika ia bersedia untuk menjadi tuan rumah sidang kemuncak Arab yang akan datang, menurut pegawai keselamatan. Amerika Syarikat pada mulanya mewajarkan pencerobohan itu dengan mendakwa bahawa rejim Saddam Hussein memiliki timbunan senjata kimia dan biologi, peluru berpandu jarak jauh, dan program senjata nuklear. Walau bagaimanapun, pemeriksaan kemudian mendedahkan bahawa walaupun Baghdad telah cuba menyembunyikan beberapa penyelidikan berkaitan senjata, Iraq sebenarnya telah dilucutkan senjata di bawah sekatan PBB pada tahun 1990-an. Pencerobohan itu dengan cepat membawa kepada kejatuhan Hussein, yang kemudiannya dihukum mati kerana pembunuhan beramai-ramai penduduk kampung Syiah berikutan percubaan pembunuhan pada tahun 1980-an. Konflik itu mengakibatkan kematian hampir 4,500 askar Amerika dan lebih 300 askar bersekutu sebelum pengunduran terakhir tentera AS pada bulan Disember. Anggaran jumlah korban Iraq melebihi 100,000.

article_content: He may have been judged a significant enough political figure to warrant a federal holiday, but some Americans seem not even to know Martin Luther King Jr. is dead. A string of pedestrians tracked down on a California street on Martin Luther King Day, Monday, claimed they had seen a speech they were told the civil rights leader gave that morning in Washington, D.C. Speaking to a cameraman for Jimmy Kimmel Live, seven of fourteen people who were asked whether they saw the supposed speech claimed to have seen it, despite King having been assassinated 46 years ago. One person seemed to keep believing in the bogus speech, even when they were asked their opinion on Beyoncé and Jay-Z having performed as backing singers during the address. A man who gave his name as Kenny Pattison, from Birkbeck, California, bluffed his way through questions about the speech, which he said was 'very inspiring, motivational' and 'current for today'. Another young man, who did not give his name but wore a blue cap and grey shirt, said he was 'shocked' at the appearance but did not question whether it happened. He was given several prompts to remember that there was no way he could have given a speech. Maybe they were dreaming? These two men were keen to discuss the speech - which did not actually happen. The person on the left suggested King could do with losing weight, while the man to the right described Jay-Z and Beyoncé's involvement in the event as 'fabulous'. How it was: Pictured above is the famous 'I Have a Dream' speech King gave, in real life, in August 1963. But while he said he was 'shocked' to supposedly see King in person at the U.S. Capitol, and admitted he hadn't 'heard him talk in a while', he never suggested it might be because he is deceased. Another responded to suggestions and said the American hero, who had parades processing in his honor at that very moment, could do with losing some weight. Introducing the segment, which aired on ABC, a bemused Kimmel said the lack of knowledge on show was 'disturbing'. He said that sometimes such videos - where they attempt to fool passers-by into saying something obviously ridiculous - often take the best part of a day to film, but this one took hardly any time. Memorial: While Kimmel's ABC show was filming the embarrassing segment, political leaders were honoring King's memory. Pictured above are a collection of politicians in front of the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial in Washington, D.C. On parade: Here activists march through the streets of Memphis, Tennessee, where King was shot dead in 1968.
translated_content: Beliau mungkin telah dianggap tokoh politik yang cukup penting untuk mewajarkan cuti persekutuan, tetapi sesetengah rakyat Amerika nampaknya tidak tahu pun Martin Luther King Jr. sudah meninggal dunia. Sekumpulan pejalan kaki yang ditemui di jalan di California pada Hari Martin Luther King, Isnin, mendakwa mereka telah melihat ucapan yang mereka diberitahu diberikan oleh pemimpin hak sivil itu pagi itu di Washington, D.C. Bercakap kepada jurukamera untuk Jimmy Kimmel Live, tujuh daripada empat belas orang yang ditanya sama ada mereka melihat ucapan yang didakwa itu mendakwa telah melihatnya, walaupun King telah dibunuh 46 tahun lalu. Seorang individu nampaknya terus mempercayai ucapan palsu itu, walaupun apabila mereka ditanya pendapat mereka tentang Beyoncé dan Jay-Z yang dikatakan membuat persembahan sebagai penyanyi latar semasa ucapan itu. Seorang lelaki yang memperkenalkan dirinya sebagai Kenny Pattison, dari Birkbeck, California, menggertak melalui soalan-soalan tentang ucapan itu, yang katanya 'sangat memberi inspirasi, motivasi' dan 'sesuai untuk hari ini'. Seorang lagi lelaki muda, yang tidak memberikan namanya tetapi memakai topi biru dan baju kelabu, berkata dia 'terkejut' dengan kemunculan itu tetapi tidak mempersoalkan sama ada ia berlaku. Dia diberi beberapa gesaan untuk mengingati bahawa tidak mungkin dia boleh menyampaikan ucapan. Mungkin mereka bermimpi? Kedua-dua lelaki ini berminat untuk membincangkan ucapan itu - yang sebenarnya tidak berlaku. Orang di sebelah kiri mencadangkan King boleh mengurangkan berat badan, manakala lelaki di sebelah kanan menyifatkan penglibatan Jay-Z dan Beyoncé dalam acara itu sebagai 'hebat'. Keadaannya: Gambar di atas ialah ucapan terkenal 'I Have a Dream' yang disampaikan King, dalam kehidupan sebenar, pada Ogos 1963. Tetapi walaupun dia berkata dia 'terkejut' kerana kononnya melihat King secara peribadi di U.S. Capitol, dan mengakui dia sudah lama 'tidak mendengarnya bercakap', dia tidak pernah mencadangkan ia mungkin kerana dia sudah meninggal dunia. Seorang lagi menjawab cadangan dan berkata wira Amerika itu, yang perarakan sedang berlangsung untuk menghormatinya pada ketika itu, boleh mengurangkan berat badan. Memperkenalkan segmen itu, yang disiarkan di ABC, Kimmel yang bingung berkata kekurangan pengetahuan yang ditunjukkan adalah 'meresahkan'. Dia berkata bahawa kadangkala video seperti itu - di mana mereka cuba memperbodohkan orang yang lalu-lalang untuk mengatakan sesuatu yang jelas mengarut - selalunya mengambil masa sehari untuk dirakam, tetapi yang ini tidak mengambil masa yang lama. Memorial: Semasa rancangan ABC Kimmel merakamkan segmen yang memalukan ini, pemimpin politik sedang menghormati ingatan King. Gambar di atas ialah koleksi ahli politik di hadapan Memorial Martin Luther King Jr. di Washington, D.C. Dalam perarakan: Di sini aktivis berarak melalui jalan-jalan di Memphis, Tennessee, tempat King ditembak mati pada tahun 1968.

article_content: One person has died and another was trapped in avalanches in the Utah mountains on Sunday afternoon, authorities stated. One of the Utah avalanches, at Snowbird Ski Resort, buried a woman under two feet of snow. She later died. Heather Gross, 27, passed away Sunday evening at a hospital in Salt Lake City due to her injuries, Salt Lake County Sheriff's Deputy Levi Hughes reported. Gross, a county resident, had been buried under two feet of snow by an early-afternoon avalanche at Snowbird Ski Resort, Hughes mentioned. Rescue teams located her approximately an hour after the avalanche, and she was transported to University of Utah hospital, where she died. A man who was with her at the time was uninjured and reported the slide, Hughes added. A second avalanche occurred nearby in the backcountry area known as Lake Desolation, according to Randy Doyle, a spokesman for the Big Cottonwood Canyon resorts nearby. He indicated that the avalanche, which left at least one person trapped, was outside the resort boundaries.

article_content: Nicola Sturgeon opened the memorial ceremony today in prayer for the ten people who died in the Clutha tragedy in Glasgow a year ago on November 29. Nicola Sturgeon led a congregation today at Glasgow Cathedral as hundreds gathered to pay tribute to those killed in the Clutha helicopter crash, one year after the tragedy. Scotland's First Minister opened the memorial ceremony in prayer while Bernard Higgins, Assistant Chief Constable of Police Scotland, shared a reading from the book of Revelation. Ten people died and many more were injured when the police helicopter, a Eurocopter EC135, crashed onto the roof of the Clutha pub in Glasgow on November 29 last year. Hundreds of people packed into pews for the ecumenical service this afternoon. Delivering the ceremony's sermon, the Catholic Archbishop of Glasgow Philip Tartaglia said the night tragedy struck at the bar began like any other Friday evening. Ska band Esperanza was playing and more than 100 people had packed into the popular Stockwell Street venue 'Clutha pub' to see them perform. Later, at about 10.25pm, disaster struck. The Police Scotland helicopter, which had been flying overhead, dropped through the single-storey building below, the Clutha pub, after both engines failed. Pilot David Traill and his passengers, police officers Kirsty Nelis and Tony Collins, lost their lives. Those killed in the pub were John McGarrigle, Mark O'Prey, Gary Arthur, Colin Gibson, Robert Jenkins and Samuel McGhee. Some 32 people were taken initially to hospitals across the city. Joe Cusker was pulled from the wreckage alive but later died in hospital. 'They have never been forgotten, especially not by those who love them most and who miss them most sorely,' Archbishop Tartaglia said. 'I can never pass by the Clutha Vaults without remembering them and recalling what happened, and whispering a 'Hail Mary' for the dead, injured and bereaved.' Audience members stood as one, as members of the mourning families lit candles in remembrance of their loved ones. The solemn Archbishop added how the tragedy had drawn Scotland together. 'Out of this tragedy we are called to be better, more compassionate, more understanding human beings,' Archbishop Tartaglia said. 'And I would hope that we could turn that memory into a legacy, a legacy which would honour the victims of the Clutha pub tragedy, so that we can say once and for all that their deaths contributed to Glasgow and Scotland becoming a better place for everyone.' Archbishop Tartaglia called for his countrymen to honour the Clutha victims' memory by making Scotland 'a place where we can all freely give what we are best at giving, according to the law and with respect for everyone's legitimate liberties, without fear and without the suspicion that we do not belong or that we are not welcome'. A man looks at floral tributes in front of the Clutha pub in Glasgow while the service was held to mark the first anniversary of the tragedy. The police helicopter crashed through the roof after its two engines failed. A child lays flowers at the memorial site for the tragedy. The crash claimed the lives of three police personnel in the Eurocopter EC135 and seven patrons in the pub which was packed for a performance by a Ska band. A family leave a heartfelt message on a floral tribute at the now closed Clutha pub. More than 100 were inside the single-storey building at the popular Stockwell Street venue when tragedy struck last November 29. 'There is a feeling around that we are in a special moment when we can shape a new Scotland,' the Archbishop added. 'In our country, no one should feel less Scots because of any part of their identity, personal, cultural or religious. We are all equal in Scotland, all welcomed, all valued, and above all, all free to express our views and follow our consciences.' 'This, I suggest, would be a Scotland which would make St Andrew would applaud, would make the Clutha Vaults victims smile with pride and would make us all happy.' Nicola Sturgeon (pictured front right) was joined by politicians, friends and family in today's memorial for the tragedy. Gatherers stood as one while members of the mourning families lit candles in memory of loved ones. Archbishop of Glasgow Philip Tartaglia, who delivered the sermon in Glasgow Cathedral (pictured), said the tragedy had drawn Scotland together and had made its people 'better, more compassionate human beings'
translated_content: Nicola Sturgeon memulakan upacara peringatan hari ini dengan doa untuk sepuluh orang yang meninggal dunia dalam tragedi Clutha di Glasgow setahun lalu pada 29 November. Nicola Sturgeon mengetuai jemaah hari ini di Katedral Glasgow ketika ratusan berkumpul untuk memberi penghormatan kepada mereka yang terkorban dalam nahas helikopter Clutha, setahun selepas tragedi itu. Menteri Pertama Scotland memulakan upacara peringatan dengan doa, sementara Bernard Higgins, Penolong Ketua Konstabel Polis Scotland, berkongsi bacaan dari kitab Wahyu. Sepuluh orang meninggal dunia dan ramai lagi cedera apabila helikopter polis, Eurocopter EC135, terhempas ke atas bumbung pub Clutha di Glasgow pada 29 November tahun lepas. Beratus-ratus orang memenuhi bangku gereja untuk perkhidmatan ekumenikal petang itu. Menyampaikan khutbah dalam upacara itu, Ketua Biskop Katolik Glasgow Philip Tartaglia berkata malam tragedi di bar itu bermula seperti malam Jumaat biasa. Band Ska Esperanza sedang bermain dan lebih daripada 100 orang memenuhi tempat popular Stockwell Street, 'pub Clutha', untuk menonton persembahan mereka. Kemudian, kira-kira pukul 10:25 malam, bencana berlaku. Helikopter Polis Scotland yang sedang terbang di atas, jatuh menembusi bangunan satu tingkat di bawah, pub Clutha, selepas kedua-dua enjinnya gagal. Juruterbang David Traill dan penumpangnya, pegawai polis Kirsty Nelis dan Tony Collins, terkorban. Mereka yang terbunuh di pub ialah John McGarrigle, Mark O'Prey, Gary Arthur, Colin Gibson, Robert Jenkins dan Samuel McGhee. Kira-kira 32 orang pada mulanya dibawa ke hospital di seluruh bandar. Joe Cusker berjaya dikeluarkan dari bangkai helikopter hidup-hidup tetapi kemudian meninggal dunia di hospital. 'Mereka tidak pernah dilupakan, terutamanya oleh mereka yang paling menyayangi dan merindui mereka,' kata Biskop Agung Tartaglia. 'Saya tidak pernah dapat melalui Clutha Vaults tanpa mengingati mereka dan apa yang berlaku, serta membisikkan 'Salam Maria' untuk yang meninggal dunia, cedera dan keluarga yang kehilangan.' Para hadirin berdiri serentak, ketika ahli keluarga yang berkabung menyalakan lilin sebagai tanda ingatan kepada orang tersayang. Biskop Agung itu menambah bahawa tragedi ini telah menyatukan Scotland. 'Melalui tragedi ini, kita diseru untuk menjadi manusia yang lebih baik, lebih berbelas kasihan, dan lebih memahami,' kata Biskop Agung Tartaglia. 'Dan saya berharap kita dapat mengubah ingatan ini menjadi warisan, warisan yang akan menghormati mangsa tragedi pub Clutha, supaya kita dapat mengatakan bahawa kematian mereka telah menyumbang kepada Glasgow dan Scotland menjadi tempat yang lebih baik untuk semua orang.' Biskop Agung Tartaglia menyeru rakyat Scotland untuk menghormati ingatan mangsa Clutha dengan menjadikan Scotland 'tempat di mana kita semua bebas memberikan yang terbaik, mengikut undang-undang dan dengan menghormati kebebasan sah semua orang, tanpa rasa takut dan tanpa syak wasangka bahawa kita tidak tergolong atau tidak dialu-alukan'. Seorang lelaki melihat karangan bunga di hadapan pub Clutha di Glasgow semasa perkhidmatan peringatan ulang tahun pertama tragedi itu diadakan. Helikopter polis itu terhempas melalui bumbung selepas kedua-dua enjinnya gagal berfungsi. Seorang kanak-kanak meletakkan bunga di tapak peringatan tragedi itu. Nahas itu mengorbankan tiga anggota polis dalam Eurocopter EC135 dan tujuh pelanggan pub yang penuh sesak untuk persembahan band Ska. Sebuah keluarga meninggalkan mesej yang menyentuh hati pada karangan bunga di pub Clutha yang kini ditutup. Lebih daripada 100 orang berada di dalam bangunan satu tingkat di tempat popular Stockwell Street ketika tragedi berlaku pada 29 November lalu. 'Ada perasaan bahawa kita berada dalam saat yang istimewa untuk membentuk Scotland yang baharu,' tambah Biskop Agung itu. 'Di negara kita, tiada siapa pun patut berasa kurang sebagai rakyat Scotland kerana mana-mana aspek identiti mereka, sama ada peribadi, budaya atau agama. Kita semua sama di Scotland, semua dialu-alukan, semua dihargai, dan yang paling penting, semua bebas untuk menyatakan pandangan dan mengikut hati nurani kita.' 'Saya berpendapat, ini akan menjadi Scotland yang akan membuat St Andrew berbangga, membuat mangsa Clutha Vaults tersenyum bangga dan membuat kita semua gembira.' Nicola Sturgeon (gambar kanan depan) turut disertai oleh ahli politik, rakan-rakan dan keluarga dalam upacara peringatan tragedi hari ini. Para hadirin berdiri serentak sementara ahli keluarga yang berkabung menyalakan lilin sebagai ingatan kepada orang tersayang. Ketua Biskop Glasgow Philip Tartaglia, yang menyampaikan khutbah di Katedral Glasgow (gambar), berkata tragedi itu telah menyatukan Scotland dan menjadikan rakyatnya 'manusia yang lebih baik dan lebih berbelas kasihan'.

article_content: During a charity polo match at Beaufort Polo Club in Tetbury, Gloucestershire, Princes William and Harry were greeted by an enthusiastic young fan with a camera phone. As they were leaving the polo field towards the changing facilities, spectators started taking photos with cameras and mobile phones. It was at this moment that the young girl took her chance, positioning herself slightly ahead of the princes with her iPhone ready. article_content: By Keith Gladdis and Claire Ellicott. PUBLISHED: 17:55 EST, 31 December 2012 | UPDATED: 06:57 EST, 2 January 2013. A primetime Channel 4 quiz in which drunken comedians made obscene jokes about the Queen has outraged viewers. The Big Fat Quiz Of 2012, which featured countless vile sexual jokes, was broadcast on Sunday only seconds after the 9pm watershed. The pre-recorded show, presented by controversial comedian Jimmy Carr, also featured puerile remarks about sprinter Usain Bolt, President Obama and singer Susan Boyle. Scroll down for video. Crude: Channel 4 has been further criticised for broadcasting Big Fat Quiz of the Year, which featured guests Richard Ayoade, Russell Howard, Jonathan Ross, Jimmy Carr, Jack Whitehall, James Corden and Gabby Logan. Last night TV watchdog Ofcom confirmed it had already received complaints. Most of the crass humour came from Gavin and Stacey star James Corden, 34, and comedian Jack Whitehall, 24, who were seen to drink a bottle of wine each on screen. They were egged on by Jonathan Ross – who left the BBC after making an abusive phone call to veteran actor Andrew Sachs during a radio show. Channel 4 last night stood accused of failing to learn from the Sachsgate scandal, which was also a pre-recorded broadcast. Margaret Morrissey, founder of campaign group Parents Outloud, said: ‘It is amazing this programme was ever broadcast. This was not live television, someone made the decision to allow this to go out at 9pm during the holidays when young children will still be up and watching television. ‘It’s as if broadcasters have learned nothing from the Sachsgate scandal. This is proof that we need a clean-up of television.’ Within minutes of the annual quiz show starting, guests began to make infantile jokes about the Queen and the Diamond Jubilee celebrations. Marlborough-educated Whitehall said he ‘had a theory’ about why the Queen had stood up throughout the Jubilee pageant on the Thames. He then made a crude joke linking it to the fact that Prince Philip was taken ill with a bladder infection soon afterwards. He justified his offensive remarks by saying: ‘I’m just saying what everyone’s thinking.’ Soon afterwards, he said Olympic gold medallist Usain Bolt could ‘rake it in’ by going to stud like the retired racehorse Frankel. His vulgar language appeared to draw gasps from the audience, but the remarks were eagerly followed up with a disgusting comment by 52-year-old Ross. Halfway through the two-hour show, Corden took a bottle of red wine and two glasses from beneath his desk and poured himself and Whitehall a drink, then started eating pizza. The pair were soon visibly drunk and Corden was slurring his words. He then started to make crude comments about Britain’s Got Talent star Susan Boyle after he was asked what hashtag was used to promote her album on Twitter. His answer was: ‘Subo loves it in the a***.’ He then laughed as he said: ‘This is where I do myself in and I forget we are recording this and this is going to be on TV’, before repeating: ‘She clearly loves it in the a***.’ Corden and Whitehall continued to get more drunk and host Carr later pointed out that the pair had drunk a bottle of wine each. Afterwards, Whitehall told his Twitter followers: ‘We got so drunk.’ Viewers took to Twitter and television forums to vent their dismay even as the programme was being broadcast. Targets: The comics made crude jokes about gold medal sprinter Usain Bolt, left, and singer Susan Boyle, right. Bad taste: Comedian Jack Whitehall made rude comments about the Queen, left, and the recent illness of her husband Prince Philip, right. One wrote on the Digital Spy entertainment website: ‘Forgive me for not laughing at people being immature idiots. But how is that comedy? It’s just inane, immature stupidity. I haven’t laughed once.’ Another added: ‘Glad Jimmy is seeing the funny side of things – as I ain’t.’ A third wrote: ‘A lot of canned laughter overlaid over the (probably) barely laughing audience. It’s a chore watching this.’ As the programme approached its conclusion, Corden and Whitehall made crass jokes about Mr Obama. Asked what the President did in the Oval Office when he was pretending to work, they responded by writing down: ‘Put a condom on and had a posh w***.’ Fellow guests sports presenter Gabby Logan, 39, and actor Richard Ayoade, 35, looked increasingly awkward as the jokes continued. On Twitter, viewers were commenting on how drunk Whitehall and Corden were. And on the Mumsnet website, one user wrote: ‘Jack and James were really annoying me with their drunken childishness. When Jonathan Ross seems like the most grown-up person there, you know it’s time to edit them out.’ Ofcom had received five complaints by last night, but that number could quickly grow – in Sachsgate, an initial two complaints rose to nearly 45,000. Former Tory MP Ann Widdecombe said: ‘Nothing Jimmy Carr does surprises me. This programme is in extremely poor taste and I’m amazed it was ever broadcast. ‘Most people would consider it to be in very bad taste to poke fun at someone in their 80s who’s served the country devotedly for 60 years.’ Mrs Morrissey of Parents Outloud added: ‘No doubt there’ll be a storm of outrage and then the comedians will turn around and be all contrite. ‘But they could have avoided offending people and corrupting young minds. Even if their parents stop them, children can still watch it on their iPads and iPhones. The nation’s television now serves the lowest common denominator.’ A spokesperson for Susan Boyle would not comment, but a source close to the singer said: ‘Their comments were inappropriate.’ A spokesperson for Corden said: ‘James would never want to offend anyone and is sorry if his comments have been taken out of the context they were made in.’ A Channel 4 spokesperson said: ‘Big Fat Quiz Of The Year is a well-established comedic and satirical review of the year’s events with well-known guests and is broadcast after the watershed with appropriate warnings.’ Channel 4 has often been at the centre of controversy. In 2007, tens of thousands complained that Bollywood star Shilpa Shetty was the victim of racist bullying on Celebrity Big Brother. Viewers also protested about a ‘dramatised documentary’ about Prince Harry in 2010 in which an actor playing the prince was shown being subjected to a mock execution in Afghanistan. Also in 2010, the broadcaster showed comedian Frankie Boyle making ‘highly offensive’ jokes about the disabled son of model Katie Price.
translated_content: Oleh Keith Gladdis dan Claire Ellicott. DITERBITKAN: 17:55 EST, 31 Disember 2012 | DIKEMASKINI: 06:57 EST, 2 Januari 2013. Sebuah rancangan kuiz waktu perdana Channel 4 di mana pelawak mabuk membuat jenaka lucah tentang Ratu telah menimbulkan kemarahan penonton. The Big Fat Quiz Of 2012, yang menampilkan banyak jenaka seks yang keji, disiarkan pada hari Ahad hanya beberapa saat selepas waktu larangan tayangan 9 malam. Rancangan pra-rakaman ini, yang dihoskan oleh pelawak kontroversi Jimmy Carr, juga menampilkan ucapan kurang sopan tentang pelari pecut Usain Bolt, Presiden Obama dan penyanyi Susan Boyle. Tatal ke bawah untuk video. Kasar: Channel 4 telah dikritik lagi kerana menyiarkan Big Fat Quiz of the Year, yang menampilkan tetamu Richard Ayoade, Russell Howard, Jonathan Ross, Jimmy Carr, Jack Whitehall, James Corden dan Gabby Logan. Malam tadi badan pemantau TV Ofcom mengesahkan bahawa mereka telah menerima aduan. Kebanyakan jenaka kasar datang daripada bintang Gavin and Stacey, James Corden, 34, dan pelawak Jack Whitehall, 24, yang dilihat minum sebotol wain setiap seorang di kaca TV. Mereka diapi-apikan oleh Jonathan Ross – yang meninggalkan BBC selepas membuat panggilan telefon yang kesat kepada pelakon veteran Andrew Sachs semasa rancangan radio. Channel 4 malam tadi dituduh gagal belajar daripada skandal Sachsgate, yang juga merupakan siaran pra-rakaman. Margaret Morrissey, pengasas kumpulan kempen Parents Outloud, berkata: ‘Sungguh menakjubkan program ini pernah disiarkan. Ini bukan televisyen langsung, seseorang membuat keputusan untuk membenarkan ini disiarkan pada pukul 9 malam semasa cuti ketika kanak-kanak kecil masih berjaga dan menonton televisyen. ‘Seolah-olah penyiar tidak belajar apa-apa daripada skandal Sachsgate. Ini adalah bukti bahawa kita memerlukan pembersihan televisyen.’ Dalam beberapa minit selepas rancangan kuiz tahunan bermula, tetamu mula membuat jenaka kekanak-kanakan tentang Ratu dan sambutan Jubli Intan. Whitehall yang berpendidikan Marlborough berkata beliau ‘mempunyai teori’ tentang mengapa Ratu berdiri sepanjang perarakan Jubli di Sungai Thames. Beliau kemudian membuat jenaka kasar yang mengaitkannya dengan fakta bahawa Putera Philip jatuh sakit akibat jangkitan pundi kencing tidak lama kemudian. Beliau mewajarkan ucapan ofensifnya dengan berkata: ‘Saya hanya mengatakan apa yang semua orang fikirkan.’ Tidak lama kemudian, beliau berkata pemenang pingat emas Olimpik Usain Bolt boleh ‘mengaut keuntungan’ dengan menjadi pejantan seperti kuda lumba bersara Frankel. Bahasa vulgarnya kelihatan menimbulkan kejutan daripada penonton, tetapi ucapan itu segera disusuli dengan komen menjijikkan oleh Ross yang berusia 52 tahun. Pada pertengahan rancangan dua jam itu, Corden mengambil sebotol wain merah dan dua gelas dari bawah mejanya dan menuangkan minuman untuk dirinya dan Whitehall, kemudian mula makan piza. Pasangan itu tidak lama kemudian kelihatan mabuk dan Corden mula bercakap tidak jelas. Beliau kemudian mula membuat komen kasar tentang bintang Britain’s Got Talent, Susan Boyle selepas beliau ditanya hashtag apa yang digunakan untuk mempromosikan albumnya di Twitter. Jawapannya ialah: ‘Subo suka dalam a***.’ Beliau kemudian ketawa sambil berkata: ‘Di sinilah saya memalukan diri sendiri dan saya lupa kita sedang merakam ini dan ini akan disiarkan di TV’, sebelum mengulangi: ‘Dia jelas suka dalam a***.’ Corden dan Whitehall terus menjadi semakin mabuk dan hos Carr kemudian menegaskan bahawa pasangan itu telah minum sebotol wain setiap seorang. Selepas itu, Whitehall memberitahu pengikut Twitternya: ‘Kami sangat mabuk.’ Penonton menggunakan Twitter dan forum televisyen untuk meluahkan rasa kecewa mereka walaupun program itu sedang disiarkan. Sasaran: Pelawak membuat jenaka kasar tentang pelari pecut pingat emas Usain Bolt, kiri, dan penyanyi Susan Boyle, kanan. Citarasa buruk: Pelawak Jack Whitehall membuat komen kasar tentang Ratu, kiri, dan penyakit baru-baru ini suaminya Putera Philip, kanan. Seorang menulis di laman web hiburan Digital Spy: ‘Maafkan saya kerana tidak mentertawakan orang yang menjadi bodoh tidak matang. Tetapi bagaimana itu komedi? Ia hanya kebodohan yang tidak matang dan tidak bermakna. Saya tidak ketawa langsung.’ Seorang lagi menambah: ‘Gembira Jimmy melihat sisi lucu perkara – kerana saya tidak.’ Yang ketiga menulis: ‘Banyak ketawa rakaman ditindih ke atas penonton yang (mungkin) hampir tidak ketawa. Ia adalah tugas yang membosankan untuk menonton ini.’ Ketika program itu menghampiri kesimpulannya, Corden dan Whitehall membuat jenaka kasar tentang Encik Obama. Ditanya apa yang Presiden lakukan di Pejabat Oval apabila beliau berpura-pura bekerja, mereka menjawab dengan menulis: ‘Pakai kondom dan melancap mewah.’ Tetamu lain penyampai sukan Gabby Logan, 39, dan pelakon Richard Ayoade, 35, kelihatan semakin kekok ketika jenaka berterusan. Di Twitter, penonton mengulas tentang betapa mabuknya Whitehall dan Corden. Dan di laman web Mumsnet, seorang pengguna menulis: ‘Jack dan James benar-benar menjengkelkan saya dengan keanak-anakan mabuk mereka. Apabila Jonathan Ross kelihatan seperti orang yang paling dewasa di sana, anda tahu sudah tiba masanya untuk menyunting mereka keluar.’ Ofcom telah menerima lima aduan menjelang malam tadi, tetapi jumlah itu boleh meningkat dengan cepat – dalam Sachsgate, dua aduan awal meningkat kepada hampir 45,000. Bekas Ahli Parlimen Tory Ann Widdecombe berkata: ‘Tiada apa-apa yang Jimmy Carr lakukan mengejutkan saya. Program ini sangat tidak sopan dan saya terkejut ia pernah disiarkan. ‘Kebanyakan orang akan menganggapnya sebagai citarasa yang sangat buruk untuk memperolok-olokkan seseorang yang berusia 80-an yang telah berkhidmat kepada negara dengan penuh dedikasi selama 60 tahun.’ Puan Morrissey dari Parents Outloud menambah: ‘Tidak syak lagi akan ada ribut kemarahan dan kemudian pelawak akan berpaling dan menjadi sangat menyesal. ‘Tetapi mereka boleh mengelakkan daripada menyinggung perasaan orang dan merosakkan minda muda. Walaupun ibu bapa mereka menghalang mereka, kanak-kanak masih boleh menontonnya di iPad dan iPhone mereka. Televisyen negara kini menyajikan tahap terendah.’ Seorang jurucakap untuk Susan Boyle tidak mahu mengulas, tetapi sumber yang rapat dengan penyanyi itu berkata: ‘Komen mereka tidak sesuai.’ Seorang jurucakap untuk Corden berkata: ‘James tidak akan pernah mahu menyinggung perasaan sesiapa dan meminta maaf jika komennya telah diambil di luar konteks di mana ia dibuat.’ Seorang jurucakap Channel 4 berkata: ‘Big Fat Quiz Of The Year ialah ulasan komedi dan satira yang mantap tentang peristiwa tahun ini dengan tetamu terkenal dan disiarkan selepas waktu larangan tayangan dengan amaran yang sesuai.’ Channel 4 sering menjadi pusat kontroversi. Pada tahun 2007, puluhan ribu orang mengadu bahawa bintang Bollywood Shilpa Shetty menjadi mangsa buli rasis di Celebrity Big Brother. Penonton juga membantah ‘dokumentari dramatisasi’ tentang Putera Harry pada tahun 2010 di mana seorang pelakon yang memainkan putera itu ditunjukkan sedang menjalani hukuman mati olok-olok di Afghanistan. Juga pada tahun 2010, penyiar itu menunjukkan pelawak Frankie Boyle membuat jenaka ‘sangat ofensif’ tentang anak lelaki kurang upaya model Katie Price.

article_content: Adam Goodes, a celebrated figure in Australian Rules Football, a sport deeply embedded in Australian culture, was subjected to a racial slur by a 13-year-old girl, an incident he found deeply offensive. As a prominent athlete in a nation where sports stars are revered, Goodes decided to address the insult directly. He recounted to CNN's "Human to Hero" series, "I stopped, confronted her, and she was escorted out. This moment significantly heightened awareness and discussions about racism in Australia." Australian Rules Football, or AFL, is described as a unique game resembling a combination of rugby codes, basketball, and Gaelic football. It mirrors Australia's ongoing struggle with its colonial legacy. While AFL has showcased instances of racial prejudice against Indigenous Australians—illustrated when a club president made a racially insensitive joke about Goodes after the girl incident, ending their friendship—it has also made considerable strides in embracing Indigenous players. This year, 68 Indigenous players are part of the 18 Premiership teams, constituting 9% of all players, a proportion exceeding the 2.5% of Indigenous people in the total Australian population. The racial abuse directed at Goodes was particularly poignant as it occurred during the AFL's 2013 "Indigenous Round" at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, a highly symbolic sporting venue with a 100,000 capacity. Goodes expressed his hope to be an example: "I aspire to be someone people admire, someone who inspires them to remember my stance at the MCG and to advocate for themselves or others who may be voiceless. Since last year, more instances of racism have been reported, which I believe is necessary for progress. Increased denouncement of racism is crucial for community improvement." In recognition of his anti-racism efforts and work with Aboriginal youth, Goodes was named "Australian of the Year" in January, coinciding with his 34th birthday. He described it as "a very humbling experience" and "an incredible platform this year to address issues close to my heart—like ending domestic violence and seeking constitutional recognition for Aboriginal people." He was surprised to learn that Aboriginal people are not recognized in Australia's constitution, a document over a century old, despite being the country's first inhabitants. When Europeans colonized Australia in the 19th century, they dispossessed Indigenous people of their land and imposed new ways of life, often forcibly separating families under the assimilation policy, a historical injustice highlighted in the film "Rabbit Proof Fence." While Australian politicians have apologized for past mistreatment, Indigenous Australians still face social and economic disparities. Goodes, like many contemporary Aboriginal people, has a mixed heritage, with a British father. Born in South Australia, his Aboriginal name is Adnyamathanha, from the Flinders Ranges region. His birthplace, Wallaroo, also connects him to the Narungga people. Reflecting on his upbringing, Goodes shared, "Growing up, my Aboriginal identity was unclear. My mother was removed from her family at age five, and we weren't taught about Aboriginal culture, language, or traditions. We knew our origins—Adnyamathanha and Narungga—but I've spent the last decade learning about it. We considered ourselves just a normal family, not mixed-race. I faced prejudice at school due to my skin color, but strong support helped me through those challenges." After his parents separated, Goodes moved to Victoria with his mother in his early teens, settling in a small town. Initially a basketball fan inspired by Michael Jordan and talented in soccer, he switched to AFL when he found no soccer teams in his new town. "I was athletic, so running was easy," he noted. "Catching the ball was harder, but I adapted quickly." AFL's basic rules involve kicking an oval ball between central posts for maximum points and outer posts for fewer points, leading to high scores. With 18 players per team in sleeveless jerseys and short shorts, the fast-paced game can be perplexing, even for those involved. Goodes joked, "You might watch and be confused, because sometimes players, coaches, fans, and even umpires are too. I'm still learning and improving; it's a game you never fully master." Though started by European settlers in the 1850s, AFL has roots in Marngrook, an ancient Aboriginal game. Goodes described it: "We played with a possum skin ball filled with charcoal, kicking and passing it over vast areas for days, with 50 players per side." Goodes's AFL accomplishments include two premierships, one as captain, and two Brownlow Medals. He believes his biggest challenge was not his Aboriginal identity in a predominantly white sport, but leaving his family at 17 to pursue his AFL dream in Sydney after being drafted by the Swans. “My first year was tough; I played in reserves all year,” Goodes recalled. “It wasn’t until the next year that I fully committed, deciding this was my path. I made sacrifices and worked hard to become a professional athlete.” He was inspired by Michael O’Loughlin, an Aboriginal teammate, whom he recently discovered is his nephew through kinship ties. O’Loughlin was the first Swan to play 300 games, a record Goodes surpassed in 2012 with his 304th game. Goodes now holds the record for most games by an Indigenous player, exceeding Andrew McLeod’s 340 games. "Michael mentored me, which was ideal, and it’s what I want for others joining football clubs," he said of O’Loughlin, who retired in 2009. After an injury sidelined him last year, Goodes is determined to prolong his career. "I know I can still improve; that’s my drive," he stated before the playoffs, where Sydney faces Fremantle after topping the season. "Some may doubt me, but I believe I have much to offer." Post-retirement, Goodes plans to focus on his foundation with O’Loughlin, providing scholarships for Aboriginal children in Sydney. "I’ve dedicated much time to my sport, leaving a void to fill," he said. "More free time will be welcome."
translated_content: Adam Goodes, seorang tokoh yang diraikan dalam Bola Sepak Peraturan Australia, sukan yang sangat berakar umbi dalam budaya Australia, telah menjadi mangsa penghinaan rasis oleh seorang gadis berusia 13 tahun, satu insiden yang dianggapnya sangat menyinggung perasaan. Sebagai seorang atlet terkemuka di negara di mana bintang sukan dihormati, Goodes memutuskan untuk menangani penghinaan itu secara langsung. Beliau menceritakan kepada siri "Human to Hero" CNN, "Saya berhenti, bersemuka dengannya, dan dia diiring keluar. Momen ini secara signifikan meningkatkan kesedaran dan perbincangan mengenai rasisme di Australia." Bola Sepak Peraturan Australia, atau AFL, digambarkan sebagai permainan unik yang menyerupai gabungan kod ragbi, bola keranjang, dan bola sepak Gaelic. Ia mencerminkan perjuangan berterusan Australia dengan warisan penjajahannya. Walaupun AFL telah mempamerkan contoh prasangka kaum terhadap Orang Asli Australia—digambarkan apabila seorang presiden kelab membuat jenaka yang tidak sensitif dari segi kaum tentang Goodes selepas insiden gadis itu, menamatkan persahabatan mereka—ia juga telah membuat kemajuan yang besar dalam menerima pemain Orang Asli. Tahun ini, 68 pemain Orang Asli adalah sebahagian daripada 18 pasukan Liga Perdana, yang membentuk 9% daripada semua pemain, satu bahagian yang melebihi 2.5% Orang Asli dalam jumlah penduduk Australia. Penyalahgunaan kaum yang ditujukan kepada Goodes sangat menyentuh hati kerana ia berlaku semasa "Pusingan Orang Asli" AFL 2013 di Melbourne Cricket Ground, tempat sukan yang sangat simbolik dengan kapasiti 100,000. Goodes menyatakan harapannya untuk menjadi contoh: "Saya bercita-cita untuk menjadi seseorang yang dikagumi orang ramai, seseorang yang memberi inspirasi kepada mereka untuk mengingati pendirian saya di MCG dan untuk menyokong diri mereka sendiri atau orang lain yang mungkin tidak bersuara. Sejak tahun lepas, lebih banyak kejadian rasisme telah dilaporkan, yang saya percaya adalah perlu untuk kemajuan. Peningkatan penolakan rasisme adalah penting untuk peningkatan komuniti." Sebagai pengiktirafan atas usaha anti-rasismenya dan kerja dengan belia Orang Asli, Goodes telah dinobatkan sebagai "Australian of the Year" pada bulan Januari, bertepatan dengan hari lahirnya yang ke-34. Beliau menggambarkannya sebagai "pengalaman yang sangat merendah diri" dan "platform yang luar biasa tahun ini untuk menangani isu-isu yang dekat di hati saya—seperti menamatkan keganasan rumah tangga dan mencari pengiktirafan perlembagaan untuk Orang Asli." Beliau terkejut apabila mengetahui bahawa Orang Asli tidak diiktiraf dalam perlembagaan Australia, dokumen yang berusia lebih satu abad, walaupun menjadi penduduk pertama negara itu. Apabila orang Eropah menjajah Australia pada abad ke-19, mereka merampas tanah Orang Asli dan mengenakan cara hidup baharu, sering kali memaksa pemisahan keluarga di bawah dasar asimilasi, satu ketidakadilan sejarah yang diketengahkan dalam filem "Rabbit Proof Fence." Walaupun ahli politik Australia telah meminta maaf atas penganiayaan masa lalu, Orang Asli Australia masih menghadapi perbezaan sosial dan ekonomi. Goodes, seperti ramai Orang Asli kontemporari, mempunyai warisan campuran, dengan bapa berketurunan British. Dilahirkan di Australia Selatan, nama Orang Aslinya ialah Adnyamathanha, dari wilayah Flinders Ranges. Tempat kelahirannya, Wallaroo, juga menghubungkannya dengan orang Narungga. Sambil merenungkan zaman kanak-kanaknya, Goodes berkongsi, "Semasa membesar, identiti Orang Asli saya tidak jelas. Ibu saya telah dipisahkan dari keluarganya pada usia lima tahun, dan kami tidak diajar tentang budaya, bahasa, atau tradisi Orang Asli. Kami tahu asal usul kami—Adnyamathanha dan Narungga—tetapi saya telah menghabiskan dekad yang lalu untuk mempelajarinya. Kami menganggap diri kami hanya keluarga biasa, bukan kacukan. Saya menghadapi prasangka di sekolah kerana warna kulit saya, tetapi sokongan yang kuat membantu saya melalui cabaran tersebut." Selepas ibu bapanya berpisah, Goodes berpindah ke Victoria bersama ibunya pada awal remajanya, menetap di sebuah bandar kecil. Pada mulanya peminat bola keranjang yang diilhamkan oleh Michael Jordan dan berbakat dalam bola sepak, beliau bertukar kepada AFL apabila beliau tidak menemui pasukan bola sepak di bandar baharunya. "Saya atletik, jadi berlari adalah mudah," katanya. "Menangkap bola lebih sukar, tetapi saya menyesuaikan diri dengan cepat." Peraturan asas AFL melibatkan menendang bola bujur di antara tiang tengah untuk mata maksimum dan tiang luar untuk mata yang lebih sedikit, yang membawa kepada skor tinggi. Dengan 18 pemain setiap pasukan dalam jersi tanpa lengan dan seluar pendek, permainan pantas ini boleh membingungkan, malah bagi mereka yang terlibat. Goodes bergurau, "Anda mungkin menonton dan keliru, kerana kadang-kadang pemain, jurulatih, peminat, dan juga pengadil pun keliru. Saya masih belajar dan bertambah baik; ia adalah permainan yang tidak pernah anda kuasai sepenuhnya." Walaupun dimulakan oleh peneroka Eropah pada tahun 1850-an, AFL berakar umbi dalam Marngrook, permainan Orang Asli kuno. Goodes menerangkannya: "Kami bermain dengan bola kulit possum yang diisi arang, menendang dan menghantarnya di kawasan yang luas selama berhari-hari, dengan 50 pemain setiap pasukan." Pencapaian AFL Goodes termasuk dua kejuaraan liga, satu sebagai kapten, dan dua Pingat Brownlow. Beliau percaya cabaran terbesarnya bukanlah identiti Orang Aslinya dalam sukan yang didominasi kulit putih, tetapi meninggalkan keluarganya pada usia 17 tahun untuk mengejar impian AFLnya di Sydney selepas dipilih oleh Swans. “Tahun pertama saya sukar; saya bermain dalam pasukan simpanan sepanjang tahun,” Goodes mengimbas kembali. “Ia tidak sehingga tahun berikutnya saya benar-benar komited, memutuskan ini adalah jalan saya. Saya membuat pengorbanan dan bekerja keras untuk menjadi atlet profesional.” Beliau telah diilhamkan oleh Michael O’Loughlin, seorang rakan sepasukan Orang Asli, yang baru-baru ini beliau ketahui adalah anak saudaranya melalui ikatan kekeluargaan. O’Loughlin adalah pemain Swan pertama yang bermain 300 perlawanan, rekod yang dilepasi Goodes pada tahun 2012 dengan perlawanan ke-304nya. Goodes kini memegang rekod untuk perlawanan terbanyak oleh pemain Orang Asli, melebihi 340 perlawanan Andrew McLeod. "Michael membimbing saya, yang sangat ideal, dan itulah yang saya mahukan untuk orang lain yang menyertai kelab bola sepak," katanya mengenai O’Loughlin, yang bersara pada tahun 2009. Selepas kecederaan menyisihkannya tahun lepas, Goodes berazam untuk memanjangkan kerjayanya. "Saya tahu saya masih boleh bertambah baik; itulah dorongan saya," katanya sebelum perlawanan playoff, di mana Sydney akan menentang Fremantle selepas mendahului musim. "Sesetengah mungkin meragui saya, tetapi saya percaya saya mempunyai banyak yang boleh ditawarkan." Selepas bersara, Goodes merancang untuk memberi tumpuan kepada yayasannya bersama O’Loughlin, menyediakan biasiswa untuk kanak-kanak Orang Asli di Sydney. "Saya telah menumpukan banyak masa untuk sukan saya, meninggalkan kekosongan untuk diisi," katanya. "Masa lapang yang lebih banyak akan dialu-alukan."

article_content: On January 3, 2012, a car accident in Logan, Utah became a story of survival and heroism. Roger Andersen lost control of his car on a winding canyon road, causing it to slide into an icy river. Inside were his daughter Mia, 9, son Baylor, 4, and their friend Kenya Wildman, 9. The car flipped and quickly submerged, trapping the children. Andersen, 46, recalling the Monday after the Saturday accident, said, 'The first thought was, "So this is it how it ends." This could have easily been a funeral for four of us.' However, quick-thinking passers-by turned potential tragedy into a rescue. Survivors Kenya, Mia, and Baylor were photographed in Logan, Utah, on Monday, showcasing their recovery. 'I was amazed at people’s readiness to jump in and help,' Andersen stated, emphasizing the critical role of the bystanders. 'Without hesitation, they did what they had to do, which made all the difference for our family.' Witnesses immediately stopped and entered the frigid river to assist. The accident occurred on Saturday as the family headed to a ski resort on a road they had traveled many times. Initially, the road seemed clear, but it became increasingly icy further into the canyon, prompting Andersen to slow down. A slight tap on the brakes triggered the slide. 'In a second, I was completely off the road and sliding down the embankment,' he recounted. 'Within a second, the vehicle cabin was full of water.' Andersen struggled to free the children from their seatbelts but couldn't. Needing air, he decided to exit the car. 'I decided the best thing was to get out and get air,' he explained. Almost instantly, about six men were on the riverbank. 'Their questions were: “Who else was in the car?” Within five seconds, eight men were in the river, ready to help,' Andersen said. The rescuers extracted the children and passed them up the bank, where CPR was administered to Mia and Baylor, who were unconscious and not breathing. They were quickly loaded into a friend’s SUV and driven towards help, meeting paramedics halfway. Mia and Baylor were airlifted to a Salt Lake City hospital, treated for hypothermia, and released on Monday. Kenya was also treated and released. 'In just a couple of days, Baylor is running around like nothing happened, Mia is fine, and Kenya is also fine,' Andersen shared. 'This story is inspiring in many ways.' He expressed a desire to become more capable of helping others, inspired by the rescuers’ actions. Kenya’s father, Dennis Wildman, described it as ‘a great story about the human spirit.' 'The bystanders literally brought our children home to us,' Wildman added, expressing deep gratitude. Former police officer Chris Willden was among the first rescuers. He used his pistol to break a car window to reach the children. 'I was trying to grab arms, but I couldn’t feel anything,' Willden recalled, describing his initial fear. He noted that about eight others descended the embankment along U.S. 89 to help. '"Hero" is not even big enough for what they did,' Mindy Andersen, Roger’s wife, stated, fighting back tears as she thanked the rescuers. Willden admitted fearing the worst. 'I remember thinking, “You’re going to see some dead kids, get ready.” I have three kids myself, and it was going to be an awful start to the New Year.' One girl was found in an air pocket, trapped by her seatbelt. Willden cut the belt with a pocket knife and pulled her out through the rear window. The other two children were rescued soon after. Mindy Andersen emotionally thanked the bystanders for saving her children’s lives.
translated_content: Pada 3 Januari 2012, kemalangan kereta di Logan, Utah bertukar menjadi kisah tentang kelangsungan hidup dan kepahlawanan. Roger Andersen hilang kawalan keretanya di jalan ngarai yang berliku, menyebabkan ia tergelincir ke dalam sungai yang berais. Di dalam kereta itu ada anak perempuannya Mia, 9 tahun, anak lelakinya Baylor, 4 tahun, dan rakan mereka Kenya Wildman, 9 tahun. Kereta itu terbalik dan tenggelam dengan cepat, memerangkap kanak-kanak tersebut. Andersen, 46 tahun, mengimbas kembali hari Isnin selepas kemalangan hari Sabtu itu, berkata, 'Fikiran pertama saya ialah, "Jadi beginilah pengakhirannya." Ini boleh sahaja menjadi majlis pengebumian untuk kami berempat.' Namun begitu, orang awam yang bertindak pantas telah mengubah potensi tragedi menjadi penyelamatan. Mangsa yang selamat, Kenya, Mia, dan Baylor telah difoto di Logan, Utah, pada hari Isnin, menunjukkan pemulihan mereka. 'Saya sangat kagum dengan kesediaan orang ramai untuk terjun dan membantu,' kata Andersen, menekankan peranan penting orang awam. 'Tanpa ragu-ragu, mereka melakukan apa yang perlu, yang membuat perubahan besar bagi keluarga kami.' Saksi-saksi segera berhenti dan terjun ke dalam sungai yang sejuk untuk membantu. Kemalangan itu berlaku pada hari Sabtu ketika keluarga tersebut dalam perjalanan ke pusat peranginan ski di jalan yang telah mereka lalui berkali-kali. Pada mulanya, jalan kelihatan jelas, tetapi ia menjadi semakin licin apabila semakin jauh ke dalam ngarai, menyebabkan Andersen memperlahankan kereta. Sedikit sentuhan pada brek menyebabkan kereta tergelincir. 'Dalam sesaat, saya sudah terkeluar dari jalan dan menggelongsor menuruni tebing,' katanya. 'Dalam masa sesaat, kabin kereta sudah penuh dengan air.' Andersen bergelut untuk melepaskan tali pinggang keledar kanak-kanak itu tetapi tidak berjaya. Kerana memerlukan udara, dia membuat keputusan untuk keluar dari kereta. 'Saya membuat keputusan bahawa perkara terbaik adalah keluar dan mendapatkan udara,' jelasnya. Hampir serta-merta, kira-kira enam lelaki berada di tebing sungai. 'Soalan mereka ialah: "Siapa lagi yang ada di dalam kereta?" Dalam masa lima saat, lapan lelaki sudah berada di dalam sungai, bersedia untuk membantu,' kata Andersen. Para penyelamat mengeluarkan kanak-kanak itu dan menghulurkannya ke atas tebing, di mana CPR diberikan kepada Mia dan Baylor, yang tidak sedarkan diri dan tidak bernafas. Mereka dengan pantas dimasukkan ke dalam SUV seorang rakan dan dibawa menuju bantuan, bertemu dengan paramedik di pertengahan jalan. Mia dan Baylor diterbangkan ke hospital Salt Lake City, dirawat untuk hipotermia, dan dibenarkan keluar pada hari Isnin. Kenya juga dirawat dan dibenarkan keluar. 'Dalam masa beberapa hari sahaja, Baylor sudah berlari seperti tiada apa yang berlaku, Mia sudah sihat, dan Kenya juga sudah sihat,' kata Andersen. 'Kisah ini sangat memberi inspirasi dalam banyak cara.' Dia menyatakan hasrat untuk menjadi lebih berkemampuan untuk membantu orang lain, diinspirasikan oleh tindakan para penyelamat. Bapa Kenya, Dennis Wildman, menyifatkannya sebagai 'kisah yang hebat tentang semangat kemanusiaan.' 'Orang awam itu benar-benar membawa anak-anak kami pulang kepada kami,' tambah Wildman, melahirkan rasa terima kasih yang mendalam. Bekas pegawai polis Chris Willden adalah antara penyelamat pertama. Dia menggunakan pistolnya untuk memecahkan tingkap kereta untuk mencapai kanak-kanak tersebut. 'Saya cuba mencapai lengan mereka, tetapi saya tidak dapat merasakan apa-apa,' Willden mengimbas kembali, menggambarkan ketakutan awalnya. Dia menyatakan bahawa kira-kira lapan orang lain turun ke tebing di sepanjang U.S. 89 untuk membantu. '"Wira" pun tidak cukup besar untuk menggambarkan apa yang mereka lakukan,' kata Mindy Andersen, isteri Roger, sambil menahan air mata ketika dia mengucapkan terima kasih kepada para penyelamat. Willden mengakui bahawa dia takut akan perkara yang terburuk. 'Saya ingat berfikir, "Anda akan melihat kanak-kanak yang mati, bersedialah." Saya mempunyai tiga orang anak sendiri, dan ia akan menjadi permulaan Tahun Baru yang mengerikan.' Seorang gadis ditemui dalam poket udara, terperangkap oleh tali pinggang keledarnya. Willden memotong tali pinggang itu dengan pisau poket dan menariknya keluar melalui tingkap belakang. Dua kanak-kanak yang lain diselamatkan tidak lama kemudian. Mindy Andersen mengucapkan terima kasih dengan penuh emosi kepada orang awam kerana menyelamatkan nyawa anak-anaknya.

article_content: Put Radiohead's Thom Yorke and Nigel Godrich, drummer Joey Waronker, the Red Hot Chili Peppers' Flea, and percussionist Mauro Refosco into a studio for three days, and you know the sound coming out of that session is going to be otherworldly. The musicians seem to have created exactly that as the band, Atoms for Peace, is edging closer to the release of its debut album, "AMOK," early next year. The move toward an album was an organic one, Yorke explains in an interview in Rolling Stone. The Radiohead singer-songwriter initially booked studio time for the group -- which was brought together to perform live songs from his 2006 album, "The Eraser" -- because of how great they sounded during rehearsal for the series of concerts in 2010. They went into their recording session with nothing, Yorke says, and ended up coming out "with a mountain." Yorke and Godrich then edited that mountain, combining it with other laptop and studio work they'd done until it turned into a nine-track album. Yorke and Godrich agree that their intent on "AMOK" was to "step into the unknown," as Godrich put it. "One of the things we were most excited about," Yorke added, "was ending up with a record where you weren't quite sure where the human starts and the machine ends." The method to creating that kind of ambiguity was its own "form of madness," Yorke recalled. "We'd go in at midday and pretty much work through to 10. We were playing all the time. It was bonkers. We'd stop to change beat. Joey and Mauro would scribe the beat out, using whatever weird notation they have, and then go off on it for another hour." Yorke's role in the process was more of a conductor, he said, as he and Godrich would pipe up with approval or disapproval of the sound's direction. "It was about trying to get interesting grooves," Yorke said. "When we first hung out, we were at Flea's house. We got wasted, played pool and listened to Fela Kuti all night. It was that idea of trancing out. But there are still songs here." Although he's tempted not to, Yorke couldn't help but remark that he "really wants to say, 'This is the beginning of something.' " Besides, "this was after three days in that studio. Imagine what they could do with a week." Will Atoms for Peace head out on tour again after "AMOK" drops? "I hope so," Yorke said. "We all want to."
translated_content: Satukan Thom Yorke dari Radiohead dan Nigel Godrich, pemain dram Joey Waronker, Flea dari Red Hot Chili Peppers, dan pemain perkusi Mauro Refosco ke dalam studio selama tiga hari, dan anda tahu bunyi yang keluar dari sesi itu pasti luar biasa. Para pemuzik ini nampaknya telah berjaya mencipta bunyi tersebut apabila band mereka, Atoms for Peace, semakin hampir dengan pelancaran album sulung mereka, "AMOK," pada awal tahun hadapan. Perkembangan ke arah penghasilan album ini berlaku secara semula jadi, seperti yang dijelaskan oleh Yorke dalam satu wawancara bersama Rolling Stone. Penyanyi dan penulis lagu dari Radiohead ini pada mulanya menempah masa studio untuk kumpulan tersebut -- yang dibentuk khas untuk mempersembahkan lagu-lagu secara langsung daripada album beliau yang dikeluarkan pada tahun 2006, "The Eraser" -- kerana mereka mendapati bunyi yang dihasilkan semasa latihan untuk siri konsert pada tahun 2010 adalah sangat menakjubkan. Mereka memulakan sesi rakaman tanpa sebarang idea khusus, kata Yorke, namun akhirnya mereka berjaya menghasilkan "sesuatu yang besar." Yorke dan Godrich kemudiannya menyunting bahan yang banyak itu, menggabungkannya dengan hasil kerja dari komputer riba dan studio yang telah mereka lakukan sebelum ini sehingga terhasil sebuah album dengan sembilan buah lagu. Yorke dan Godrich bersetuju bahawa tujuan mereka dalam menghasilkan "AMOK" adalah untuk "meneroka sesuatu yang tidak diketahui," seperti yang dinyatakan oleh Godrich. "Salah satu perkara yang paling kami teruja," tambah Yorke, "adalah menghasilkan sebuah rakaman yang membuatkan anda tertanya-tanya di mana bermulanya elemen manusia dan di mana berakhirnya elemen mesin." Kaedah untuk menghasilkan suasana yang samar-samar seperti itu dianggap sebagai "sejenis kegilaan" oleh Yorke. "Kami akan masuk ke studio pada tengah hari dan bekerja berterusan sehingga pukul 10 malam. Kami bermain muzik sepanjang masa. Ia memang gila. Kami hanya berhenti seketika untuk menukar rentak. Joey dan Mauro akan mencatat rentak tersebut, menggunakan apa jua sistem notasi unik yang mereka ada, dan kemudian meneruskannya untuk satu jam lagi." Yorke menggambarkan peranannya dalam proses ini lebih kepada seorang konduktor, kerana dia dan Godrich akan memberikan maklum balas sama ada mereka menyukai atau tidak arah bunyi yang dihasilkan. "Tumpuan kami adalah untuk menghasilkan rentak yang menarik," kata Yorke. "Ketika kami mula-mula berkumpul, kami berada di rumah Flea. Kami minum hingga mabuk, bermain biliard, dan mendengar lagu-lagu Fela Kuti sepanjang malam. Dari situ, tercetuslah idea untuk menghasilkan muzik yang menghanyutkan. Namun, album ini masih mengandungi lagu-lagu yang berstruktur." Walaupun pada mulanya dia agak keberatan, Yorke akhirnya mengakui bahawa dia "benar-benar ingin mengatakan, 'Ini adalah permulaan bagi sesuatu yang baharu.' " Tambahan pula, "semua ini terhasil selepas tiga hari di studio. Bayangkan apa yang mampu kami lakukan jika kami mempunyai masa selama seminggu." Adakah Atoms for Peace akan mengadakan konsert jelajah lagi selepas pelancaran "AMOK"? "Saya harap ya," jawab Yorke. "Kami semua memang mahukannya."
